module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 224

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/224](https://www.erdosproblems.com/224)
- [DaGr62] Danzer, L. and Gr\"{u}nbaum, B., *\"{U}ber zwei Probleme
  bez\"{u}glich konvexer K\"{o}rper von P. Erd\H{o}s und von V. L. Klee*.
  Math. Z. (1962), 95-99.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos224

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

/-- The angle $yxz$ is obtuse. -/
def ObtuseAt {d : ℕ} (x y z : ℝ^d) : Prop :=
  inner ℝ (y - x) (z - x) < 0

/--
If $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is any set of $2^d+1$ points then some three points in $A$ determine an obtuse angle.

The general case was proved by Danzer and Gr\"{u}nbaum [DaGr62].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos224.lean"]
theorem erdos_224 {d : ℕ} (A : Finset (ℝ^d)) (hcard : A.card = 2 ^ d + 1) :
    ∃ x y z : ℝ^d, x ∈ A ∧ y ∈ A ∧ z ∈ A ∧
      x ≠ y ∧ x ≠ z ∧ y ≠ z ∧ ObtuseAt x y z := by
  sorry

end Erdos224

reformulations.difference: The geometric condition is expressed as a negative inner product, equivalently an angle strictly greater than π/2. This includes a straight angle rather than imposing an additional upper bound strictly below π.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The cited paper explicitly describes the original condition as every angle being at most a right angle (p. 95); its violation is therefore an angle greater than π/2, including π. For nonzero displacement vectors, the inner product is the product of their positive norms and the cosine of the angle, so negativity is equivalent to this condition. Repeated-point cases cannot satisfy the predicate. In scratch Lean proofs, ObtuseAt x y z ↔ π/2 < EuclideanGeometry.angle y x z was proved for all points and dimensions, as was equivalence of the theorem's full conclusion with geometric angle existence.

review.notes:
Both declarations were checked; no mathematical defects were found. The d=0 extension is harmless: ℝ^0 is a singleton, so A.card = 2^0 + 1 is impossible. The cardinality hypothesis was proved satisfiable for every positive dimension. Lean tests also checked repeated points and concrete acute, right, obtuse, and straight angles.

The source records PROVED (LEAN), affirmative, matching both metadata attributes. The linked proof has the same statement and compiled with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound after three local compatibility adjustments from its declared Lean/Mathlib v4.29.1 to the sandbox version. All experiments are under /workspace/review/.

Direct access to erdosproblems.com was blocked. Its prose/status were read through the text proxy; because that rendering omitted formulas, the mathematical bound and angle convention were independently checked in the cited primary paper's full GDZ OCR text.
